messages:
Elena (prod): quick sync — need to agree ordering for Optimize toolkit features: quantization, batching improvements, and prefix/KV caching. customers asking for all three; we only have 2 sprints.
Raj (eng-runtime): can we assume batching improvements give the biggest unit-cost win for request-heavy customers? iirc throughput x2 for streaming cases.
Priya (eng-ml): quantization reduces memory and GPU perf for larger models — big wins for Dedicated customers who hit memory limits. but it's more engineering risk.
Tess (cs): the SMB customers keep asking for lower per-token cost (they care about price). enterprise customers ask for predictable latency and caching for repeated prompts.
Marco (sre): caching also reduces load spikes and improves SLO during bursts. it's lower risk than quant, but ops complexity depends on eviction policy.
Elena (prod): proposing we score by RICE-ish: reach (customers impacted), impact (unit-cost or latency), confidence, and effort. quick draft:
Elena (prod): - Batching: R=high, I=medium-high (cost), C=high, E=low-medium
Elena (prod): - Caching: R=medium, I=medium (latency + cost during repeats), C=high, E=medium
Elena (prod): - Quantization: R=medium, I=high (cost/throughput for large models), C=low-med, E=high
Raj (eng-runtime): that aligns with our perf numbers. batching is easiest to prototype (continuous batching tweaks + kernel selection). quant will need new code paths + more validation.
Priya (eng-ml): one nuance: quant gives diminishing returns on smaller models; it's mainly for >7B. our hosted catalog is mixed.
Tess (cs): customers doing embeddings (SMB) would see less benefit from quant. they benefit a LOT from batching and caching.
Marco (sre): if we pick batching first, we can also ship ops controls (per-route batch windows) that help Dedicated customers tune latency.
Raj (eng-runtime): suggestion: do batching (sprint A) + light caching primitives (LRU, prefix cache for common prompts) in parallel by pairing a backend engineer and a PM. quantization as a focused spike in sprint A with demo; full rollout in sprint B if spike looks good.
Elena (prod): timeline proposal: sprint A = batching + basic cache + quant spike; acceptance = 10-20% unit-cost reduction for target workloads OR cache hit-rate >= 15% with no regression to p95 latency.
Priya (eng-ml): for the quant spike we should set success criteria: model size reduction, perf delta, and a small eval on quality regressions (prompt set). otherwise it wastes time.
Tess (cs): can we surface a customer beta for caching early? want to put a few power users on it to validate hit patterns.
Elena (prod): yes — Tess will recruit 3 customers. Raj/Priya will own spike telemetry. Marco will own rollout runbook (fallback to non-quantized model).
ops-bot: "Reminder: roadmap planning meeting Fri 09:00 — add final decision" :calendar:
Elena (prod): next steps: Raj to estimate effort for batching (2d dev + 1d testing), cache proto (3d), quant spike (5d). Priya will draft eval suite. Tess will surface customers. we'll reconvene Thu for final prioritization.
Raj (eng-runtime): noted. I'll post a quick RFC with perf numbers + minimal config options.
Priya (eng-ml): adding note: if quant spike shows >6% quality regression we pull the brake and prioritize caching instead.
Tess (cs): customers OK with early beta; will get back with names by EOD.
Elena (prod): thanks all — trying to avoid scope-sandwich. goal: measurable wins in sprint A and a clear go/no-go for quant before committing sprint B. :thumbsup:
